existing_issues.issue: Year 1957; PWM first published 1961; no duration listed
Duration is 11 min and year 1994 per publisher list (catalogue says 10 min)
Title could read 'Concerto No. 1 "Tālā gaisma" (Distant Light)'; year 1996-97, 30 min confirmed; accompaniment is string orchestra (piano reduction exists)
Duration 12 min (catalogue 10); year 1999 (rev. 2006); accompaniment is string orchestra (not 'Strings')
Duration 24 min (catalogue 20); year 2008-09; piano reduction with solo part exists (Schott VLB 148)
Schott: 'Dedication, symphony for violin and orchestra', 1990-91, 40 min (catalogue says 35); only hire material is listed (no piano reduction found)
Schott gives duration 15 min and year 1991 (catalogue 18 min)
Silvestrov's 'Three Postludes' (BEL 619) is for soprano, violin, cello and piano, and 'Postludium' is a symphonic poem for piano & orchestra; no solo-violin Postludium No. 2 found
'Two Pieces' (Walzer, Weihnachtsserenade): Schott lists 'Walzer und 2 Serenaden' (BEL 853, 2012, 3 min) as piano solo; no violin version found. Check 1267-1269

Existing 'Suite on Estonian Dances' appears to be ETW 53 'Suite on Estonian Dance Tunes' (violin & piano, 1943/1952; Körling c1952 as 'Trois danses populaires esthoniennes'), not the 1979 solo suite; consider title 'Suite on Estonian Dance Tunes'
Programme source gives year 2012 and duration about 6 min (catalogue 4 min); title also spelled 'Impuls' in the Sikorski edition
